title: Journal of Computational Physics
Published by
The Fourier Spectral Transformer for efficient and generalizable nonlinear PDEs
Article preview
Abstract
Keywords
abstract:
Abstract
In this work we propose a unified Fourier Spectral Transformer network that integrates the strengths of classical spectral methods and attention based neural architectures. By transforming the original PDEs into spectral ordinary differential equations, we use high precision numerical solvers to generate training data and use a Transformer network to model the evolution of the spectral coefficients. We design two complementary sequence models for the evolution of spectral coefficients, a Fourier Spectral Transformer and an exponential time difference Transformer. The latter embeds the analytic linear propagator of the PDE through an exponential time differencing update, while a Transformer is used to learn the nonlinear contribution. We evaluate the proposed Transformer with Burgers’ equation, two-dimensional and three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. The numerical experiments show that the models achieve highly accurate long-term predictions from relatively limited training data, and that the exponential time difference Transformer exhibits improved stability and convergence. The proposed Transformer generalizes well to unseen data, bringing a promising paradigm for real time prediction and control of complex dynamical systems.

  - heading "Introduction" [level=2]
  - generic: The partial differential equations solving is a cornerstone of computational science and engineering, which can be computationally expensive, especially when dealing with high-dimensional, nonlinear, and complex systems.
  - generic: In recent years, machine learning has emerged as a powerful tool to address these challenges, particularly through the integration of data driven models with physics based constraints. The key development in this area is Physics Informed Neural Networks, which incorporate PDE residuals and boundary and initial condition penalties directly into the loss function of a neural network, unifying forward and inverse problem solving [1]. The comprehensive survey of physics-informed machine learning elucidates the connections between PINNs, neural operators, neural differential equations, and outlines future challenges [2]. PINNs in Fluid Mechanics [3] reviewed the application of PINNs in fluid mechanics, summarizing their performance on Navier-Stokes, Burgers’, and other flow problems, and discussing practical aspects like loss weighting and adaptive sampling. The adaptive activation in PINNs [4] introduced adaptive activation functions in PINNs, showing that dynamically learned nonlinearities can accelerate convergence and improve accuracy for stiff PDEs. Hidden Fluid Mechanics [5] showed how PINNs can infer hidden fluid dynamics recovering velocity and pressure fields purely from sparse flow visualizations thus making non intrusive flow diagnostics from image data.
  - generic: The Neural operators have emerged as another significant advancement. These models, such as the Fourier Neural operator, learn the solution operators for parametric PDEs by performing convolution in the Fourier domain [6]. The introduction of Dealiasing Fourier neural operator further improves numerical precision by correcting spectral aliasing errors, a key limitation in high frequency domains [7]. Deeponet, a framework for learning nonlinear operators between function spaces, also provides universal approximation capabilities for parametric PDEs [8]. The Graph Kernel Network[9] is an early operator learning framework that laid the groundwork for Fourier neural operator. Kovachki et al. [10] provided a unified theoretical analysis of neural operators including Fourier neural operator, Deeponet, and GKN highlighting their approximation properties. Gupta et al. [11] proposed a multiwavelet based operator learning approach, extending the spectral operator paradigm to wavelet bases. Pathak et al. [12] applied Fourier neural operator in FourCastNet for high resolution global weather forecasting, demonstrating state of the art predictive performance. Li et al. [13] combined Fourier neural operator with physics constraints to form the Physics Informed Neural operator. Lu et al. [14] conducted a comprehensive benchmark of deep operator networks, comparing Fourier neural operator against alternatives on unstructured PDE problems and analyzing architectural tradeoffs.
  - generic: There are other important contributions including Sinusoidal Representation Networks which use periodic sine activation functions to significantly improve the ability of neural networks to model high frequency signals and solve differential equations improving the approximation of implicit fields and high frequency components [15], [16], [17], [18]. The Transformers for PDEs explore the use of attention based architectures to model non-local interactions in PDE solutions, offering a promising method for dealing with complex dependencies between variables [19]. The integration of classical methods with neural networks has led to the development of Learned Iterative Solvers, which combine neural networks with traditional iterative solvers to accelerate convergence while maintaining physical consistency [20].
  - generic: The deep learning methods for partial differential equations have evolved from pointwise approximations to increasingly sophisticated operator learning frameworks. The developed stable neural flows tailored to the dynamics of differential equations [21]. The physics informed neural networks were extended to parametric and high dimensional PDEs, making forward and inverse modeling with embedded physical constraints [22], [23], [24], [25], while error analysis and gradient pathology studies provided a more rigorous understanding of their numerical behavior [26], [27]. The parallel efforts focused on learning solution comprehensive surveys and methodologies on neural operators [28], physics informed Deeponets [29], and operator networks robust to general coordinate transformations [30] established a unifying perspective on operator learning for PDEs. Practical toolkits such as DeepXDE [31] helped standardize implementations, and related advances in adaptive coordinate networks and nonlocal neural PDE solvers further improved representation power for complex geometries and nonlocal interactions [32], [33].
  - generic: The Transformer based learners such as the [34] have begun to unify these ideas within attention based architectures solving a broad class of PDE problems. The Transformer architecture was introduced in 2017 as an attention alternative to recurrent and convolutional sequence models for machine translation [35]. Several works have introduced physics informed Transformers which treat samples as sequences and use attention to capture non local interactions [36]. Recently, hybrid machine learning general circulation models have been proposed to bridge the gap between purely data driven weather models and traditional physics based GCMs. NeuralGCM combines a differentiable dynamical core that solves the moist primitive equations with neural network parameterizations of unresolved physical processes [37]. Building on these developments, we design a Transformer based architecture aiming to combine the attention with physical constraints for accurate and robust PDE solutions under diverse conditions. The Transformer we build is very accurate in prediction and training comparing to the literatures.
  - generic: The machine learning methods have not yet surpassed traditional numerical approaches in terms of accuracy. In particular, convergence and stability analyses remain limited compared to those available for conventional numerical methods, and predictive accuracy outside the training domain is insufficient. We introduce a Fourier Spectral Transformer network and exponential time difference transformer. The results demonstrate that they have the potential for accurate long term prediction after training. The neural network is capable of producing highly accurate predictions even when trained on relatively limited data. Its ability to generalize from sequences makes robust forecasting of future velocity fields with minimal computational cost a significant advantage. The network effectively captures the flow dynamics throughout both the training and prediction intervals, proving its potential as a powerful tool for solving complex fluid dynamics problems.
